fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`ready_tickets` is bounded at 90,000 bytes by bug `daughterly-agitative-ocelot`
(`494b-2dd3-e9d3-4fb0`), but even after that fix's lean projection it sits at **58 rows /
87,893 wire bytes — roughly ONE row of headroom**. The bound is correct and its refusal is
actionable (it points at `next_batch`), but the tool will begin refusing its default call
about as soon as one more ticket becomes ready. That is a cliff, not a fixed problem.

`ready_tickets` is a discovery surface: it answers "what can I work on next?" A discovery
caller needs id, alias, title, type, status, priority, and blocking summary, not dependency
arrays, file-impact arrays, authorship, comments, or full ticket defaults. Measured on the real
store (58 ready rows, 90,000-byte budget):

| shape | bytes/row | rows that fit | headroom vs today |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| as shipped (lean, `TicketStateOut`) | 1,515 | 59 | +1 |
| lean minus `file_impact`/`deps`/author/env fields | 801 | 112 | +54 |
| summary fields, still via `TicketStateOut` | 572 | 157 | +99 |
| summary fields via a NEW closed output model | 234 | 384 | +326 |

Two findings drive this:

1. **The lean ready row still carries fields a discovery caller cannot use.** `file_impact` is
   252 B/row (18.1% of the row) and `deps` 160 B/row (11.5%) — 30% of the payload between them,
   for a question that only needs discovery fields and blocking state.
2. **`TicketStateOut`'s declared defaults set a floor.** Projecting to summary fields but
   returning `TicketStateOut` still costs 572 B/row, because `model_validate` re-adds
   `description: null`, `comments: []`, `deps: []`, `inbound_deps: []`, `file_impact: []`,
   `file_impact_scope`, `no_file_impact_reason`, `plan_review_health: null` and
   `cross_session_warning: null`. **338 of those 572 bytes are re-added defaults** — the same
   mechanism that made the parent bug's budget under-estimate by 178%.

## Approach

Implement the durable fix: change the default `ready_tickets(full=False)` MCP response to a new
closed discovery output model with exactly the fields needed for choosing work (ticket id, alias,
title, type, status, priority, and blocking summary). Keep `ready_tickets(full=True)` returning the
existing full `TicketStateOut` shape for callers that explicitly opt in to full details. This
mirrors common actively maintained OSS API practice: list/discovery endpoints return compact item
summaries, while detail or explicit-expanded calls return the complete resource.

Do not change `list_tickets` in this ticket. Its filters make an over-budget refusal actionable,
so the budget is a guardrail there; `ready_tickets` has no narrowing arguments and needs a safer
default shape. Document the output narrowing as its own release note and changelog entry because a
new output schema is a declared contract change rather than just another field omission under the
`494b` axis.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py` — select the discovery model for default `ready_tickets` and retain
  the full model when `full=True`.
- `src/rebar/_mcp_models.py` — define the closed discovery output model/schema.
- `src/rebar/schemas/ready_ticket_summary.schema.json` — add the canonical schema file for the
  new public output model.
- `src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py` — adjust only if the shared read projection needs a
  matching discovery field set.
- `docs/output-schemas.md` — update generated/schema documentation if the new public model changes
  the output-schema inventory.
- `docs/release-notes.md` — record the output contract narrowing and the `full=True` escape hatch.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — add the user-facing changelog note.
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_list_payload_budget.py` — add the per-row-size regression.
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_output_schema_coverage.py` — update the `ready_tickets`
  canonical default schema and add/retain coverage that `full=True` validates as `TicketStateOut`.
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_list_read_surface.py` — replace default-shape parity with the
  deliberate asymmetry: `list_tickets` remains filterable/full enough by default, while
  `ready_tickets` defaults to discovery and `ready_tickets(full=True)` remains full.
- `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_model_schema_drift_heldout.py` — keep model/schema drift
  coverage current for the new public output model if the inventory requires an explicit example.
- `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_schema_outputs.py` — keep typed read-tool output schema coverage
  aligned with the ready-tickets default schema change.

## Testing

- RED first: add a regression in `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_list_payload_budget.py` that
  fails on current `main` because default `ready_tickets` rows exceed the discovery per-row ceiling
  after `model_validate` and `js_safe_result`.
- Happy path: default `ready_tickets` returns discovery-shaped rows and the measured wire payload has
  at least 3x current-store headroom.
- Compatibility path: `ready_tickets(full=True)` still returns full `TicketStateOut` rows with fields
  such as `deps`/`file_impact` available.
- Schema wiring: `test_mcp_output_schema_coverage.py`, `test_mcp_model_schema_drift_heldout.py`,
  and `test_schema_outputs.py` pass with the new canonical discovery schema.
- Documentation: release notes and changelog name the contract change and the `full=True` escape
  hatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A decision is recorded on the ticket to use a new closed discovery output model for default
      `ready_tickets`, with `full=True` continuing to return full `TicketStateOut` rows.
- [x] Default `ready_tickets` has headroom for at least 3x the current ready count on this store,
      measured on the wire payload after `model_validate` and `js_safe_result`; verified by a
      regression test in `tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_list_payload_budget.py`.
- [x] The new public discovery output model has a canonical schema file and the MCP schema coverage
      tests validate default `ready_tickets` against that schema.
- [x] `ready_tickets(full=True)` remains compatible with the previous full `TicketStateOut` shape and
      is covered by a contract/read-surface test.
- [x] The output-schema change is recorded in `docs/release-notes.md`.
- [x] The output-schema change is recorded in `CHANGELOG.md`.
- [x] `list_tickets` is explicitly left unchanged because its filter arguments make over-budget
      refusal actionable; this asymmetry is documented in the change.
- [x] Regression coverage asserts the per-row size ceiling so default ready rows cannot silently
      re-grow.
